title: A ‘wellhead-to-water’ delivery network for Permian crude producers
summary: Enbridge’s US$600M acquisition of Salt Creek Midstream gathering assets establishes full-path solution to tidewater, using Gray Oak and Enbridge Ingleside Energy Center export terminal
body_markdown:
Enbridge just added the capstone piece of a strategic Permian puzzle—all the way from wellhead to water.


On Aug. 26, we announced the **[acquisition of Salt Creek Midstream’s crude oil gathering business](https://www.enbridge.com/media-center/news/details?id=123886&lang=en)** —500 miles of pipeline, with a combined 420,000 barrels per day of output capacity—in West Texas and New Mexico for US$600 million.


The gathering network **[ties directly to long-haul Permian egress pipelines](https://www.enbridge.com/~/media/Enb/Documents/Investor-Relations/2026/ENB_2026_09_09_Acquisition_of_Premier_Crude_Infrastructure.pdf#page=5)** —including Enbridge’s **[majority-owned Gray Oak Pipeline](https://www.enbridge.com/map#map:infrastructure,search=%22850-mile%20Gray%20Oak%22)** , and the **[Cactus II line](https://www.enbridge.com/map#map:infrastructure,search=%22Cactus%20II%20Pipeline%20system%22)** in which we have a 30% ownership stake—which in turn deliver Permian oil to the Enbridge Ingleside Energy Center, North America’s largest crude export terminal.


As a result, Enbridge can now offer West Texas producers pillar-to-post service in reaching customers around the world, bring more U.S. domestic crude to export markets, and continue to serve global demand for responsibly sourced energy.
